issues.text: The evaluator questions whether KLS's results are robust to the choice of comparator class, since rotavirus is the only comparator used; alternative vaccine comparators could yield different counterfactual coverage estimates.
issues.quote: there is a reasonable worry over whether the results are robust to a different comparator class of vaccines when estimating the counterfactual impact

issues.text: The evaluator's own analysis relies on heterogeneous, disparate datasets (WUENIC, UNICEF, Shearer et al.), so the comparisons across vaccines are not on a consistent basis and the results are very rough; the evaluator cautions against direct comparison with KLS's findings.
issues.quote: The disparate datasets are not ideal, but no single source I found while undertaking this quick review provides comprehensive data on all vaccines of relevance.

issues.text: Yellow fever coverage data are very limited (only 2000 and 2010 available), so the linear interpolation and extrapolation used to fill other years introduces substantial uncertainty into the YF comparator estimate.
issues.quote: Only 2000 and 2010 vaccination rates were available from the source I found; both WHO and the International Vaccine Access Center/John Hopkins View-Hub project were not forthcoming

issues.text: Treating missing country-year data as 0% coverage is a methodological choice that may bias coverage estimates downward; the evaluator flags the considerable amount of missing data and the assumption underlying it.
issues.quote: the datasets used see a considerable amount of missing data; in such cases, I made the methodological choice to treat missing data for country-years as 0%

issues.text: The weighting scheme for the comparator classes is subjective and aggressive, with weights assigned by judgement, making the derived 11% counterfactual coverage estimate uncertain.
issues.quote: Weights are assigned subjectively and fairly aggressively, with each penalty leading to a comparator class being weighed a magnitude less than it otherwise would have.

issues.text: KLS's DALY averted estimates may overstate benefits because DALYs per capita from pneumococcus were already declining before the AMC, and projections based on past burden data do not account for this secular trend.
issues.quote: DALYs lost per capita to pneumococcus were declining in poor countries year-on-year for two decades even before the AMC, possibly due -- at least in part -- to economic growth

issues.text: KLS do not model the possibility that the AMC accelerated development of existing nearly-licensed vaccines, which would mean the counterfactual timing of introduction is not captured; the evaluator considers this speculative and hard to test.
issues.quote: KLS do not model the speeding up of the development of existing vaccines -- hypothetically, the credible commitment provided by the AMC will have a dynamic effect

issues.text: The evaluator argues the estimate of lives saved (700,000) is uncertain; while confident the AMC made a difference, they have only moderate confidence in the specific headline figure.
issues.quote: (b) only moderate confidence that at least 700,000 lives were saved, per KLS's original estimate.
